title: Assurance gating & cadence: SSO, audit logging, and SOC2/ISO readiness
creator: Priya Shah
description: This ticket consolidates the milestone gating plan, cadence, and acceptance criteria for our 2026 assurance priorities: SOC2 Type II readiness, ISO27001 alignment, SSO/SAML enterprise integrations, and platform-wide audit logging. The goal is to create an executable milestone roadmap with clear gates, owners, and artifact checklists so engineering, security, and product can coordinate releases without last-minute audit scope changes.
objectives: Define a 6-week milestone cadence linking engineering deliverables to audit artifacts
Create pass/fail gating criteria for SSO (SAML + OIDC) integrations to support enterprise onboarding
Standardize audit logging schema and retention plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments
Map SOC2 and ISO controls to concrete deliverables and owners (technical + process)
Surface dependencies early to legal, infra, and solutions engineering teams to avoid audit delays
milestones: M1 (2026-02-25): SSO gating checklist finalized; test plan and integration spec published
M2 (2026-03-15): Audit logging MVP schema implemented in runtime + console views; retention policy draft
M3 (2026-03-31): SOC2 control mapping doc complete; evidence collection templates created
M4 (2026-04-15): ISO27001 gap analysis complete with remediation owners assigned
M5 (2026-04-30): Dry-run evidence package for core controls and SSO audit simulation
acceptance_criteria: SSO: End-to-end SAML flow validated with test enterprise org; SAML metadata and cert rotation documented
Audit Logs: Events emitted for auth, token issuance, model execution, and admin actions; logs exportable to SIEM
SOC2/ISO: Each mapped control has at least one piece of supporting artifact (doc, dashboard, or test) and an assigned owner
Release gating: No security-related release can proceed without updated evidence links in the milestone tracker
risks: Late discovery of cross-region data retention regulatory requirements could change retention windows
Third-party SAML provider quirks may require per-customer mapping work and extend integration timelines
Evidence collection burden on SEs if artifacts are not templated and automated
Parallel feature launches (runtime perf changes) could alter logged event shapes and delay validation
rollout_plan: Adopt a two-track cadence: an engineering sprint track that delivers technical artifacts and a compliance track that validates artifacts, performs dry-run audits, and updates control mapping. Each milestone has a gating checklist: (1) tech artifact exists, (2) test evidence uploaded, (3) owner sign-off, (4) compliance review. Use biweekly milestone syncs with Security and Solutions to unblock external integrations.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Security and Runtime. Agreed on gating template and evidence catalog. Action: Security to draft control mapping by 2026-02-18.
2026-02-18: Control mapping first pass received from Security; identified 14 technical controls requiring instrumentation. Action: ENG owners assigned.
2026-02-24: SSO checklist draft completed. Engineering to implement SAML metadata verification and cert rotation endpoints. Assigned to ENG-4298.
2026-03-01: Audit log schema v0.1 implemented in runtime branch. Integration tests failing on event ordering; Mateo investigating.
2026-03-05: Dry-run plan documented; external auditor scoping call scheduled for 2026-03-22. Need confirmation from Legal on NDA for auditor.
2026-03-05: Updated milestone dates after risk review; extended M2 by one week to allow for event shape stabilization.
notes: Keep milestone artifacts machine-readable where possible (YAML/JSON) to simplify evidence export to auditors.
Coordinate with Solutions to create a customer-facing SSO onboarding checklist that mirrors internal gating requirements.
Consider a small automation spike to pull logs into evidence bundles for SOC2 evidence collection.
